name: Attack the king in the centre
mnemonic: Uncastled king + open centre = open lines straight at it.
principle: When the enemy king hasn't castled, open the centre — even at the cost of material — and bring every piece into play before it can escape.

moves.note: Double attack on f7 and b7: the king is still on e8.
Develop first — every new attacker counts.
Pin the defender of d7/e5.
Sacrifice to rip open lines to the king.
Castle with tempo: the rook hits the pinned knight.
The final sacrifice deflects the knight.
Morphy, 1858: Black's kingside pieces never moved.

points: Count developed pieces: if you have three more in play, sacrifices often work.
Open files and diagonals towards the king (Nxb5, Bxb5+).
Pins on the defenders paralyse the defence.

name: The Greek gift (Bxh7+)
mnemonic: Bishop takes h7, knight to g5, queen to h5.
principle: Against a castled king with no knight on f6, sacrifice the bishop on h7, then bring the knight and queen with tempo.

moves.note: Conditions: pawn on e5 (no ...Nf6), knight can reach g5, queen can reach h5.
Threat: Qh7 mate. Black has no defender for h7.

points: Check the three conditions before you sacrifice.
The knight on g5 and queen on h5 form the mating net.
If the king runs to g6, h4–h5 or Qd3+ keep the attack going.

name: Opposite-side castling: pawn storm
mnemonic: Kings on opposite wings? Throw your pawns at theirs — fast.
principle: When kings castle on opposite sides, pawn advances don't weaken your own king. Push pawns to open files against the enemy king, and trade off its best defender.

moves.note: The Yugoslav Attack set-up: Be3, f3, Qd2, O-O-O.
Kings on opposite sides: the race is on.
Open the h-file with h4–h5.
Next: Bh6 or Bxf6 to remove the key defenders of the black king.

points: Pawn moves near your own king are dangerous; near the enemy king they are weapons.
Trade the defender: Bh6 removes the g7-bishop.
Count tempi: the side that opens a file first usually wins.

name: Trade off the defender (Bh6)
mnemonic: No fianchetto bishop, no defence on the dark squares.
principle: A fianchettoed bishop is the king's best guard. Exchange it, put your queen on h6 and open the h-file.

moves.note: Offer to trade the g7-bishop — the guardian of the dark squares.
The queen lands next to the king.
h4–h5 opens the h-file for the rook.

points: Remove the defender before you attack.
The h-file is the highway once h5 and hxg6 happen.
Ng5 often joins with mate threats on h7.

name: Sacrifice on f7
mnemonic: f7 is guarded only by the king — hit it early.
principle: Early in the game f7 (f2 for Black) is the weakest square. A sacrifice there can drag the king into the open.

moves.note: Two attackers on f7.
Natural, but a mistake (5...Na5! is correct).
The Fried Liver sacrifice.
Check and pressure on the pinned d5-knight.
More attackers: the d5-knight is pinned and attacked three times.

points: Attack the weakest square with more pieces than defend it.
After the sacrifice, keep giving checks and bringing pieces.
Defence: develop, castle, and don't open the centre with your king there.
